Review Title: The *custom tour* you’ve been looking for.
Review Text:
If you can afford it, do it. If you can’t afford it - do it anyways and make cuts to other things (eating out, shopping, etc)

My husband and I wanted to celebrate our 1st anniversary and be just a little bit extra. We have always had a fascination with the Farallon Islands (about 20-30 miles west off the Bay Area coast) but the only way to get there was by plane or seriously-rough-boat ride (for whale spotting).

I called and spoke with *Anna* who was very patient and explained for a private tour I would have to more-or-less buy out the whole plane. And there was no guarantee I would see the Farallons.. we may just get close. I talked it over with my husband and decided, even though the price point was far out of our budget, we would not be so extravagant in future anniversaries/events, and to make this one special.

Anna called the day-of and explained the weather to be too rocky for us to get a clear view. No problem, we are from SF, I’m a student pilot, and we understand how temperamental the weather can be up here. We rebooked for the following day.

TODAY we drove up, met Anna, who is absolutely lovely, and wait for the plane to return for us to depart. You dont realize it but Anna has to literally ‘catch’ the plane from the dock and both of them jump off and pull the plane in to secure. I saw Anna carefully sanitize all areas of the plane, and our pilot, Fred, did a preflight inspection (checked propellor, gas, etc.) even though they had just landed. We felt very safe boarding the flight.

Not only was Fred knowledgeable and experienced he was great to speak with about general aviation. We didn’t expect to get very close to the Farallons but Fred managed to fly us over them, around them (not once but three times at varying banks!) and made sure we got all the photos we needed. Watching the Farallons from the air was magical. Though a little dizzy, and having spent all our time to fly out and back, we were ecstatic and had an absolute blast.

Fred took our photos upon landing (one of the smoothest landings EVER), and even shook my hand and told me to come back after I got my private so I could learn how to handle a seaplane (they fly beavers).

This was an absolutely AMAZING experience, especially because we were able to achieve our custom flight path. Fred and Anna went above and beyond.

You BET I’m coming back after I get my private to get my seaplane rating. Thank you again for an experience AND anniversary we won’t soon forget!!

Review Title: Seaplane Tour + Alcatraz Tour in afternoon
Review Text:
We booked this trip because it also provided us with two tickets to Alcatraz once the Seaplane Tour had ended. We were picked up in front of the Hard Rock Cafe at 9:00 am. The van was on time.
We then drove to the Seaplane base in Sausalito, signed the necessary forms and boarded with two other couples. Each person has a window seat. We flew over the Golden Gate Bridge, Alcatraz prison, AT&T stadium, Muir Woods and SanFrancisco city itself. Our pilot, John , has been flying for over 50 years. He was great and all of us felt comfortable with him at the controls. I only have one suggestion that the company write a two or three sentence description of each place John points out. Otherwise he really does not have the time to elaborate on each point of interest we were flying over.
Each person wears earphones to keep engine noise to a minimum and provide a communication link between the pilot and passengers. If you ask a question speak loudly into the microphone provided. It’s voice activated and needs a strong voice to activate it .
Management worked very hard with the Hotel Zoe Concierge, Aiyaz Ali, to confirm our flight and the two Alcatraz tickets. Everything worked out fine. The flight lasted a half hour and John flew us over most areas twice so passengers on both sides of the plane had the same quality view and the ability to take photos with their cameras or smart phones. Once the trip was over , the pilot borrowed our cameras and took pictures of each couple standing on one of the pontoons. We were then driven back across the Golden Gate Bridge again and dropped off at the Hard Rock Cafe. We then walked down to the Alcatraz pier and exchanged our vouchers for afternoon tickets to The Alcatraz prison. You will need to show a photo ID to pick up the Alcatraz tickets and show that ID again twice when you board the afternoon ferry.

Review Title: Little too laid back pickup, but very cool flght
Review Text:
We realized too late that we wanted Alcatraz tickets, so we booked the combo package with Seaplane Adventures. We waited over an hour in the sun for our pickup, without any notification from the company. That started us off in an irritable frame of mind. The pickup driver didn't apologize, he just kept "explaining" that traffic was really bad because of an event. Letting us know so we could stroll around or do other things would have helped that a lot.

Once we got there, check in was smooth and the pilot, John, was pleasant and low key. The ride itself was terrific. John went to the places we could see (there were lots of clouds and fog) and had some interesting comments about the sights. He tilted the plane to the left and right to give us better views of some places of interest. The landing was very neat, and the return drive was ok.

We had to ask like five or six questions for the driver to tell us we just needed photo ID to pick up our Alcatraz tickets. Had we known this when we were waiting for pickup, we could have saved time and frustration.

The cool factor of the seaplane ride itself outweighed these silly problems, but they could have been avoided.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: What a Kick in the Pants!
Review Text:
The hour long flight is a blast. I thought we'd just tool around the Bay, but we headed up the Marin headlands past Mt. Tam to Tomales Bay & Pt. Reyes. The trip back south took in Pt. Bonita and the old batteries. You get a good view of both lighthouses without the long trek down the bluff. On a clear day (which we had) you can see out to the Farallons, and you'll get to do some whale and pinniped watching if you're lucky.
Aaron, the pilot, points out the sights and gives a bit of history and context along the way. I can vouch for his familiarity with the area and its history. You're likely to learn a bit, even if you grew up in Northern California and made it through fourth grade CA history.

I was only in town for 48hrs on business so wanted some big-hitting tours to see as much as possible during my stay in the city. I love flying anyway and when I found that I could fly in a seaplane and the legendary Dehavilland Beaver at that, I knew it was the best option.

I did the coastal tour which is an hour duration and also arranged the taxi collection from Pier 39 - all of which went smoothly. Graced by some great weather, the tour was fantastic from start to finish. I actually went on my own but confirmed beforehand that this would be okay - two other tourists were on the flight.

The pilot deserves special praise as a fantastic tour guide who was informative and very entertaining despite the fact he must do the tours hundreds of times every year. He also thought nothing of deviating from the tour a little or circling landmarks just so we could get a better view.

The aerial views of the miles of coastline, the bridge, city and Alcatraz are exceptional and you simply can't see everything we saw in less than three or four days, yet we did it all in an hour. For me, it's an essential trip if you're in town, even if you're staying for longer. Just make sure the weather forecast is good.

Pilot was brilliant. Funny, informative and always keeping an eye on the customers. My daughter it turns out isn't a great flyer, so he kept a close eye on her.

Whole flight was brilliant and then we got an extra small car tour on our return of a few key SA sights on route back to Fishermans Wharf.

We then had 3 hours before our Alcatraz tour to grab lunch and wander.

It's worth knowing that you get your tickets for Alcatraz from the Tour Desk not the Pre Booked desk, as we wasted a bit of time in the wrong queue !

Alcatraz is an absolute must on a SA visit. Fantastic tour of a part of American history.

My teenagers were fine and enjoyed the audio tour and got a real insight into the prison.

I'd been 20+ years ago but still enjoyed the trip, nothing much was different though 😀

We chose 45 minute flight which on a clear day was definitely right decision. It takes a few minutes to really relax and it gave me time to enjoy taking in the instruments and mechanics of flying this old plane as well as the views - and what views. Pilot was informative and funny and was happy to answer questions ( goegraphical and aeronautical) . Having been up and down the coast at sea you then fly right over the Bridge and along the city frontage before turning right over the City and heading back over Alcatraz. Always just a hint of nerves as you land but smooth and safely down. Back on the mooring pontoon a chance to pose for pictures standing on the float of "your" seaplane! The whole thing is a real treat for boys ( and girls) from 6 to 66!

Review Title: Very poor and indifferent customer service.
Review Text:
Visited San Francisco for 5 nights in early Feb 2015. Phoned Seaplane Adventures from my hotel, and spoke to a man. I asked if there were any flights tomorrow ? Man said there might be a weather front coming in, phone back tomorrow morning. The next day, I phoned several times to be told, " all our agents are busy, or it's after hours, and ring back or leave a message". I left a message, and gave my name , hotel and room number. No reply. The next day, I phoned again, and the phone just kept ringing and ringing, no answering machine kicked in. The next day, we decided to drive out to the Mill Valley office, saw the sea planes parked up, in the mud, but the office was closed. I enquired at an adjacent office, and was told that " there's usually someone there by 10 'ish". At around 10.15am, a red pick up arrives with Seaplane Adventures written on the side. We go into the office only to be told that they're not flying today. In fact, due to low customer demand, they rarely fly from December through March !
So San Francisco doesn't get tourists from December through March ? I asked the owner?, Why don't you mention this on your advertising material ? Why don't you reply to messages left on your answering machine ? We have wasted time in attempting to contact you, and wasted time and fuel driving to your base, and for what ? The man didn't really have much to say, so we left.
Exiting the seaplane office. I saw a helicopter land alongside, so I thought, what about a helicopter trip instead of a seaplane trip. The passengers got out of the helicopter and walked to a tour bus. I asked the driver, " how much are the helicopter flights ?". He didn't have a clue. The helicopter had shut its engine down, so I walked towards the helicopter when the pilot motioned me to halt, whilst he was speaking on his mobile phone. I waited nearly TEN MINUTES for him to finish his call, he got out, and I asked " when's the next flight ?". He said, "about 2.00pm 'ish ". He asked how many passengers there would be, I explained two. He said, in that case he would have to charge me for FOUR persons. Excuse me, you want to charge me almost one thousand US dollars for a 30 minute flight around San Francisco ? Needless to say, we left. In fact, we left so fast, I didn't have time to note the name of the helicopter company, but they're situated next door to Seaplane Adventures, 242 Redwood Highway, Mill Valley, SFO.

Review Title: Fantastic way to see San Francisco and wonderful experience
Review Text:
Having visited SF 2 years ago and seen everywhere from ground level we wanted to do something that was that little bit more special and something we had never done before.

In one word it was AWESOME. The weather that day was brilliant with unexpected unrestricted views (no haze) and the sea was like a mill pond. Getting in a plane that is parked on water is an experience in itself and once the safety brief was carried out the taxi to the take off point and the take off itself was a wonderful visual and emotional experience. It is difficult to describe what it is like as the aircraft accelerated to take off speed, skimming across the sea as it did so.

Once airborne our decision to take the flight was rewarded a thousand times and more. Words can not describe the excitement of looking down on San Francisco, The Golden Gate, Alcatraz, The Piers and all the other areas and attractions we flew over. Our pilot made this a very personal experience despite the number of flights he had already made and he provided us with a good description and information on all the parts of our flight.
As with all experiences the 45 minutes were soon gone and it was back to base and a landing experience that was all as good if not better than the take off.
I had done a few hundred flights when I did skydiving as a hobby so I was used to being in a small plane but that did not dull the experience of taking off and landing on water it really is one for the bucket list. If you haven't done it yet trust me you MUST.

My wife on the other hand has little or no experience of small planes and was a little nervous prior to the flight BUT she loved every minute and would have gone back to do it again. She said she always felt safe and trusted both the aircraft and pilot!

Thanks to everyone at Seaplane Adventures, this was a special birthday experience for me and you made it a stunning one.

Review Text:
My family purchased this as the morning part of my birthday celebration - total surprise.

We were picked up promptly at Fishermans Wharf and quickly transported to their base in comfort. Have to say the morning started with a dense SF fog but a quick phone call advised us not to worry as it would lift - and it did.

Aaron, the pilot, was superb with a running commentary all the time, pointing out interesting sights as we came towards them. Occasionally he would fly around so people on both sides could view items. We covered the Mill Valley/Marin towns on the way to the lower Wine Valleys the traversed the Bay to cover SF, Alcatraz and GG Bridge.

This was a superb way to see the area from a different perspective and in an old seaplane. We were speedily transported back to Pier 39 afterwards. A very professional outfit with nice people. No hesitation in recommending.

Review Text: We did this trip on the 17th of October.  We were picked up at Pier 39 on time and driven straight to Sausilito where the seaplane took off.  It was pretty foggy as we drove over the Golden Gate Bridge so I wasn't really sure what we would see when we were up there.  Anyway, we were taken straight away and we did the hour tour and shared with another couple of people.  The pilot was very engaging and entertaining and we totally enjoyed our flight.  We felt very safe the whole time, which was especially important for my husband who isn't too keen on heights!  We flew over the vineyards, surrounding towns and the views over the Golden Gate were absolutely mesmerising.We managed to get some amazing photos, some with the fog, some without.  Once the flight was over we were driven back to Pier 39, no hanging around whatsover.  Would not hesitate to recommend this company, they are first class.

Review Text:
My partner and I took this trip, booked through Viator, in September, during our 3 day stay in San Francisco, while travelling California. We were picked up efficiently and on time from Pier 39, by a friendly and engaging driver, who happily pointed out local sights for us both on the way to Mill Valley, where the seaplane is based and back again. This guy was so informative and helpful, he even stopped twice on the way back so we could take photos of Landmark sights.
The flight itself was great! Our pilot Aaron, was clearly very skilled, confident and experienced in flying the plane. He made sure that everyone (there were four passengers in total, maximum would be five) could ask any questions they had, using the headphones with mikes and gave a really good commentary of the areas we were flying over, throughout the roughly 40 minute flight. I was really lucky in being 'co-pilot', sat at the front. This meant that I was able to lower the window beside me from time to time, to take photos without glass between the camera and the outside world. Having said that, the glass was very clear, so other than possible reflections, pictures would have come out really well anyway. We happened to be flying on the last day of the Americas Cup race and being one of only three airborne vehicles (the other two being media helicopters) made the experience even more special, our pilot making the most of this occasion for his fortunate passengers.
Overall, a very highly recommended trip and very good value for money!

Review Title: Fantastic experience and great way to see this beautiful city
Review Text:
Aaron picked us up from Pier 39 for our seaplane flight, he was very punctual and there exactly on time. As he drove us to the seaplane, he pointed out all the interesting things to look at on the way,and gave us information about the all the things we saw. He knows the area very well and is very happy to share his knowledge.

When we arrived we saw the beautiful seaplane and Aaron explained to us how to get on safely and was happy to take a photo of us in front of the plane before take off. Once in the plane he told us what to look at as we were taking off, and once airborne he gave us great information on all we saw, and pointed out where to look.

The day we flew was magnificent and we had a birds eye view of the bridge, the city, the stadium, Alcatraz, the house boats, Sausalito and some of the magnificent homes on the foreshore. Aaron's personal commentary let us know where to look, and when to get the camera ready, and provided us with interesting facts and history about what we saw.

At all times we felt very safe, and thoroughly enjoyed our flight.

On the drive back Aaron dropped us off at Sausalito and showed us where to catch the ferry back. He also suggested many good places to have lunch. We took his advice and enjoyed a lovely Mexican meal at one of the restaurants.

This is truly a great way to see this beautiful city, and I would highly recommend this tour, it was a very memorable experience and Aaron was an excellent pilot and guide.

Review Text:
This is a must do in San Francisco. The views are spectacular and incredible. Riding in seaplane is lot of fun.
The address on their web site is not accurate and our GPS took us to a wrong place. We called their number several times even before we left for the tour but no one answered. We thought we were ripped off and not many people are aware of this place in the neighborhood. We had to ask some stranger to find this place. They didn't even care to say sorry or being considerate. This is a family owned place and there is only one old lady to take care of all so she doesn't seem to care that much.
Anyway take Mill Valley-Stinson exit on 101 North and you will see the Seaplanes on your right , make a right at Pohono St and make right again on Bolinas St. GPS co-ordinates to Pohono St [37.87953, -122.51497].
Regardless it's a great tour and I recommend this place as it is not crowded and there is plenty of parking space.
We took the 30-min $170 golden gate tour. We flew in a 6-seater seaplane over Marin Headlands, turned & flew over golden gate bridge (an awesome view), fly close to city skyline and then headed back to Sausalito. It felt really short but it was lot of fun esp. landing and takeoff, which was very smooth.

We had quite a windy and gusty but clear day, taking off at 5pm - the wind made the ride particularly exciting! The impressive de-Havilland and our pilot pilot rode a path with spectacular views from Sausalito to Muir Beach, down to the lighthouse and across Golden Gate park, over to the Giants gamepark, over the city and back over Tiburon - all the while the pilot mixing a few local facts with cheeky jokes. Highly recommended.
